figures.alt: Photo of an eroding sandy bluff on Lake Michigan with fallen trees at its base and waves washing the shore.
figures.caption: Waves and wind wear the shore away. Erosion moves the pieces.

figures.alt: Photo of a cliff with horizontal layers of tan and gray rock and a small shell in one layer.
figures.caption: Rock layers build up over time, usually older at the bottom. A shell fossil is evidence of a past environment.

figures.alt: Photo of a plastic tray with a sand shoreline, a row of stones along part of the shore and a cup of water.
figures.caption: A model shoreline: test a barrier with the same amount of water each time and compare the sediment lost.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Sediment moved by waves. No barrier 12 spoonfuls, Wall 7 spoonfuls, Grass 5 spoonfuls.
figures.caption: Sediment lost in the shoreline tray: no barrier 12 spoons, wall 7 spoons, grass 5 spoons.
